title: The Eve of the Finals
next_chapter_hook: Su Qingyao's fingertips trembled slightly as she finally revealed the secret sealed away for years—the hidden blood connection between her and Chen Ji's deceased father.

text.content: The night was dark as ink, and thin frost clung to the eaves of the Tianqing Sect. Chen Ji sat alone in the Servants' Quarters, the candlelight flickering, casting his lean profile in alternating light and shadow. The scene of Ling Yuan being stripped of his qualification still replayed in his mind—the old sect master's hunched back, etched with hatred, like a dull knife that cut repeatedly at Chen Ji's heart. He knew it wasn't enough. Ling Yuan had built his power in the sect for decades; how could one defeat bring him down completely? However, what truly chilled Chen Ji's heart was that flash of crimson light beyond the crowd. Han Lie. The number one prodigy of the Xuanwu Sect. The killing intent in those eyes was almost solidifying into substance.

"Knock, knock, knock—" Three knocks, with distinct rhythm, piercingly sharp in the silent night. Chen Ji frowned slightly. At his current situation, a late-night visitor definitely spelled trouble. He gently closed the "Tianqing Heart Method" in his hand, his fingertips tapping twice unconsciously on the cover. "Who is it?" No answer came from outside the door. Chen Ji rose, his footsteps almost soundless. He deliberately made his breathing heavier, his footsteps becoming unsteady—the signature posture of a废物. Even knowing it might be a trap, he had to let the other party see a timid Servant Disciple.

dialogue.content: Creak—the door opened. Chen Ji hunched his back, squinting as he peered outside, his lips trembling: "Who, who is it? It's the middle of the night..."

text.content: Under the moonlight, a tall and slender figure stood quietly outside the door. Her white dress fluttered slightly in the night breeze, like a sliver of cold moonlight. The visitor's face was exquisitely beautiful, yet as cold as millennium-old glacial ice—precisely Su Qingyao, the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow of the Tianqing Sect. Chen Ji's heart tightened, but his expression revealed a mixture of surprise and panic: "S-Su Senior Sister? Why are you..." He stepped back half a pace. "What brings you here in the middle of the night?"

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao gave no answer, her gaze sweeping across Chen Ji's face like a blade. After a long moment, she spoke coldly: "Let's talk inside." Before Chen Ji could react, she had already slipped through the door gap, bringing with her a waft of cold, ethereal fragrance.

text.content: Chen Ji closed the door. The moment he turned around, a sharp light flashed in his eyes. Su Qingyao's late-night visit was no coincidence. This Inner Disciple Senior Fellow was one of the figures he guarded against most—she was extremely observant, her mind meticulous, discovering clues in details time and time again. "Please sit, Senior Sister." Chen Ji brought over the only wooden stool, his voice still trembling. Su Qingyao did not sit. Instead, she produced a letter from her sleeve and slapped it onto the table. "Someone delivered this tonight." Her voice carried no warmth. "Addressed to you."

Chen Ji's gaze fell upon that letter. An ordinary white paper envelope, the seal without any wax stamp. He picked up the envelope, and the moment it touched his hand, his fingertips trembled slightly— That handwriting. So familiar it nearly suffocated him. It was his father's handwriting. Chen Ji's breath caught. He slowly drew out the letter paper. Only a few lines, the characters dignified and solemn, exactly matching his father Chen's former writing style. "Ji'er, tomorrow at the finals, be careful with everything. Someone is setting a trap, intending to take your life."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji stared at those few characters, his expression shifting from shock to confusion, then quickly contained. "Father's handwriting..." he murmured to himself, his voice carrying just the right amount of bewilderment. "But Father already... How could this be possible?" He raised his head, eyes brimming with tears: "Senior Sister Su, where did this letter come from?"

Su Qingyao watched his performance coldly. She had seen too many such gazes—appearing cowardly on the surface, but hiding a blade beneath. "I didn't see the messenger." Her voice was平静, almost cruel. "But this letter was mixed in with my private correspondence... The sender knew my address very well, and also knew the relationship between us." She stepped forward, staring directly into Chen Ji's eyes: "What do you think this means?"

text.content: Chen Ji lowered his eyes, concealing the cold light within. This letter was forged. Though the handwriting resembled it, it lacked his father's unique pause strokes—that detail cultivated over years of copying scriptures, impossible for outsiders to imitate. But someone capable of threatening him with his father's handwriting was no ordinary person. He knew what the mastermind behind this wanted: fear. To make him mentally destabilized by this letter, revealing weaknesses during the finals. Unfortunately, they had targeted the wrong person.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, folding the letter paper and tucking it into his chest. "Thank you for the reminder, Senior Sister." His voice recovered some composure. "Regardless of who is behind this scheming, Chen Ji will not back down." Su Qingyao's brow furrowed: "You still intend to participate in tomorrow's finals? Do you know..." She suddenly stopped, seemingly hesitating whether to continue.

text.content: Just then, the Tianji Record Fragment in Chen Ji's chest suddenly grew warm. It was a familiar sensation—Tianji was warning him. Chen Ji's expression remained unchanged, but his heart was already churning like a tempest. He made an excuse to pour tea, turning his back to Su Qingyao, secretly retrieving the fragment. Golden light flowed across his palm. "Divine three hours ahead." The characters on the fragment flickered faintly. Chen Ji gritted his teeth, injecting a wisp of divine sense into it— Heavenly Fate Value, -5.

The scene exploded before his eyes. In the center of the finals venue, under the cloudless arena platform, the sunlight was blinding. Chen Ji saw himself standing on the platform, facing a crimson figure—Han Lie. The Xuanwu Sect's prodigy's twin fists burned with flames, killing intent seething in his eyes. Yet the next moment, the stone pillars at the four corners of the platform suddenly lit up with an eerie glow. A massive formation rose from the ground, enveloping the entire arena. That was... a Lethal Trap Formation. Within the formation, Han Lie advanced with a sinister grin. And Chen Ji discovered that his spiritual energy within was completely suppressed, not even a trace could be mobilized.

The scene continued. Han Lie's iron fist smashed into Chen Ji's chest, the sound of shattering bone clearly audible. Blood sprayed from Chen Ji's mouth, staining his white garments crimson. He wanted to flee, but there was no escape. He wanted to resist, but not even the strength to raise his arm remained. Han Lie looked down at him, lips moving, uttering a few words— "A废物 should老老实实stay in the mud." Then came another punch. Chen Ji watched himself on the platform collapse to the ground, his pupils gradually dimming. Death. True death.

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji!" Su Qingyao's voice pulled him back from the illusion. Chen Ji opened his eyes abruptly, discovering he was gripping the table's edge, cold sweat beading on his forehead. He quickly tucked the fragment back into his sleeve, forcing a bitter smile onto his face. "Sorry for making Senior Sister witness this. I just... remembered Father, feeling a bit sad." Su Qingyao's gaze lingered on his face for a long while, seemingly discerning truth from falsehood. "What did you just see?" she suddenly asked, her voice carrying a trace of imperceptible tension.

text.content: Chen Ji's heart tightened. She noticed? "I won't hide it from Senior Sister." Chen Ji sighed. "I am indeed hesitating about whether to participate in tomorrow's finals. Father's letter... though I don't know if it's real or not, I'd rather believe it exists." He raised his head, meeting Su Qingyao's gaze with open eyes: "Senior Sister specifically came to warn me, surely it's not just about that letter?"

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao fell silent for a moment. Moonlight filtered through the window lattice, casting dappled shadows on the floor. She stood with hands behind her back, facing away from Chen Ji, her voice suddenly dropping lower. "The platform for the finals has been tampered with." Chen Ji's eyes flickered slightly: "What kind of tampering?" "Formation bases were buried beneath the four stone pillars." Su Qingyao's voice was cold as frost. "Once activated, it will form a lethal killing formation, turning the arena into a Deadly Ground." She turned around, her gaze burning as she stared at Chen Ji: "Someone wants you to die there quietly and without fanfare."

text.content: Chen Ji slowly sat down, his expression showing genuine shock. "Why tell me this, Senior Sister?" His voice was somewhat hoarse. "As far as I know, you've always suspected me. Tonight you came, wanting to see how I end up?" Su Qingyao did not deny it. "That's right." Her voice was soft, yet candid. "I do suspect you. But before that—" She paused, seemingly weighing her words. "You cannot die on tomorrow's arena platform."

These words came too suddenly. Chen Ji was stunned. He looked into Su Qingyao's eyes, trying to find even a trace of hypocrisy or scheming, but only found... exhaustion. Deep exhaustion. And an inexplicable obsession of some kind. "Senior Sister, we've only met a few times." Chen Ji slowly spoke. "Why would you risk so much for a废物 disciple?" Su Qingyao gave no answer. She walked to the window, gazing at the crescent moon in the night sky, her back appearing somewhat desolate. "Because... someone asked me to."

dialogue.content: "Asked you?" Chen Ji's brow furrowed. "Who?" Su Qingyao turned around, moonlight carving cold contours on her face. Chen Ji watched her, waiting for the answer. Yet just then, Su Qingyao's expression suddenly changed. She cocked her head to listen, her expression shifting drastically. "Someone is coming." She grabbed Chen Ji's wrist and pulled him toward the window: "Go, leave from the back." Before Chen Ji could react, the window lattice had already been shattered by Su Qingyao's palm strike. The two of them slipped out the window, disappearing into the night.

text.content: The moment they landed, Chen Ji glanced back. At the door of the Servants' Quarters, two black shadows were silently approaching. Had it not been for Su Qingyao's vigilance, they would already be caught in an encirclement. Those two figures wore night clothes, their eyes beneath face coverings gleaming with a ghastly light—the aura of assassins. Su Qingyao did not pause, pulling Chen Ji as they darted between the rooftops. "There's an ambush." she whispered. "Tonight's situation is more complicated than I thought." Chen Ji let her pull him along, but his mind was racing at lightning speed. Threatening letter, lethal trap formation, nighttime assassination— Three-pronged attack. This was a scheme to erase him completely.

The two stopped in an abandoned alchemy room. Su Qingyao released his hand, her expression returning to its usual coldness: "It seems you can't go back tonight." Chen Ji surveyed their surroundings—crumbled alchemy furnaces, dusty meditation cushions, and even curtains of spider webs in the corners. This place clearly had been neglected for ages. "Thank you for saving my life, Senior Sister." He clasped his hands in a formal bow, his voice sincere. Su Qingyao waved her hand dismissively: "No need for thanks. I just don't want to owe anyone a favor." She paused, her gaze complicated as she looked at Chen Ji: "What do you plan to do about tomorrow's finals?"

dialogue.content:
Su Qingyao's eyes flickered with surprise at Chen Ji's decision.

"Are you certain?" Her voice carried less coldness. "Withdrawing from the finals means giving up this chance for fame. So many would covet such an opportunity."

Chen Ji forced a bitter smile: "What's the point of reputation if you're dead?"

Su Qingyao's gaze transformed.

It was no longer scrutinizing, but something ineffably radiant—as if she had finally glimpsed something long awaited.

"You intend to step into the Deadly Ground?" she softly echoed, her voice carrying an unexpected hint of amusement. She stepped closer, near enough that Chen Ji could detect her subtle fragrance: "What's your plan?"

dialogue.content:
Su Qingyao's lips curved upward at his words.

"Removing the fuel from beneath the cauldron?" she murmured. "I appreciate this approach."

She withdrew a token from her sleeve, waving it before Chen Ji: "An Inner Disciple Senior Fellow's token, capable of redirecting patrol schedules in the sect's western region for half an hour."

"Plus me," she pocketed the token, her gaze sharp as a blade. "Two is sufficient."

text.content:
Chen Ji listened quietly, his eyes glinting. He understood Su Qingyao was testing him. The so-called "plan" was merely performance for her benefit. Yet her token held genuine utility—the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow's authority could ensure their movements went unnoticed for half an hour.

"Thank you, senior sister," he cupped his hands. "If we truly can destroy the formation bases, Chen Ji would be profoundly grateful."

Su Qingyao studied him, seemingly gauging the truth in his words. After a moment, she turned toward the door.

"Follow. While the night is still dark."

Chen Ji tailed her, a subtle smile playing on his lips.

This woman... proved more intriguing than he'd imagined.

Two silhouettes slipped through the darkness, evading patrol after patrol. Su Qingyao's knowledge of the sect's layout was impeccable, each turn precise. Chen Ji trailed behind, committing the route to memory.

A quarter-hour later, the finals Arena Platform materialized before them. The massive stone platform gleamed coldly under moonlight, four towering pillars carved with intricate patterns. Without the Tianji Record's forewarning, the concealed lethal formation would have been invisible.

Su Qingyao halted at the Arena Platform's edge, whispering: "The formation bases lie three feet beneath the pillars. You take the eastern and western pair; I'll handle the southern and northern."

She glanced at Chen Ji: "Remember, work swiftly. Once the formation activates, no one within ten zhang survives."

Chen Ji nodded, darting silently toward the eastern pillar. His movements were feather-light, landing without a sound. The pillar's patterns shimmered faintly in moonlight as Chen Ji focused his senses, detecting the concealed spiritual fluctuation—the formation base directly beneath.

Pressing one palm to the ground, he projected his consciousness downward.

A jet-black formation disk lay embedded in blue stone, bristling with dense restriction runes. Once activated, it could transform a ten-zhang radius into a death zone.

"Ruthless," Chen Ji's gaze chilled.

The formation's destructive potential could obliterate any cultivator below the Golden Core stage. The scheme's architect had left absolutely no room for survival.

Chen Ji drew a steadying breath, channeling spiritual energy to his fingertips.

Two methods existed for dismantling a formation base: brute-force destruction, which risked triggering alarms, or subtlety—locating the formation disk's weak point and carefully disarming its restrictions.

He chose the latter.

Knowledge from the Tianji Record flooded his mind—a page previously unsealed by Mo Xiansheng, documenting various formation-breaking techniques.

"Found it."

His fingertip precisely targeted a specific point on the formation disk, gently entwining spiritual energy.

Click.

A faint sound emerged as the runes on the disk dimmed, and the spiritual fluctuation vanished.

The eastern pillar's trap: neutralized.

dialogue.content:
Simultaneously, a soft sound came from Su Qingyao's location.

"Done." She glided to Chen Ji's side, expression composed. "The southern and northern bases are destroyed."

Chen Ji gave a slight nod: "The western one is mine."

Just as he prepared to move, his brow furrowed—

Footsteps echoed in the distance.

Multiple persons.

Su Qingyao detected the anomaly too, gripping Chen Ji's wrist and yanking him into the pillar's shadow.

"Stay quiet," she breathed, her voice barely audible, her exhalation warm against Chen Ji's ear.

text.content:
Chen Ji held his breath, peering through the pillar's gap.

Three dark silhouettes emerged from the shadows, halting at the Arena Platform's edge. One carried a bronze mirror, its surface gleaming with an eerie green light.

"Strange," the man frowned. "Two formation disks have lost their presence."\

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji and Su Qingyao hid in the shadows behind the stone pillar, pressed extremely close together.

Su Qingyao's body was slightly stiff, clearly unaccustomed to such intimate proximity. But she didn't move, only lowering her breathing to its minimum.

Chen Ji could sense the faint ethereal fragrance emanating from her, along with her slightly accelerated heartbeat.

The footsteps grew closer and closer.

One of the black shadows was walking toward the stone pillar where they were hiding, the light from the bronze mirror in his hand growing brighter and brighter.

Three zhang... two zhang...

Su Qingyao's hand quietly gripped the sword hilt at her waist.

text.content:
Just then—

"Whoosh!"

A piercing sound came from the distance, followed by a muffled grunt.

The black shadow approaching them猛地 turned around, and beside another stone pillar on the opposite side, a white figure was slowly dissolving.

"It's a feint!" someone hissed.

Without hesitation, the three black shadows gave chase, quickly vanishing into the night.

Su Qingyao and Chen Ji exchanged a glance, both seeing confusion in each other's eyes.

That white figure... who was it?

"Let's go." Su Qingyao whispered, "While they're away, let's complete the final step."

Chen Ji followed Su Qingyao as she glided toward the western stone pillar.

His heart stirred with waves of emotion—the white figure's movement technique, he seemed to have seen it somewhere before. That lightness like a butterfly, that evasiveness like the wind, made him inexplicably think of someone.

But now was not the time for contemplation.

He pressed his palm against the ground, his spiritual sense probing into the formation disc.

The formation foundation here was more complex than the eastern one, with layers upon layers of prohibitions, clearly the work of a master. But before the knowledge of the Tianji Record, these prohibitions were merely puzzles awaiting solution.

After an incense stick's time, the formation foundation beneath the western stone pillar was also dismantled.

"All complete." Chen Ji straightened up, fine beads of sweat on his forehead.

Su Qingyao checked the surroundings, confirming nothing was missed, then signaled Chen Ji to leave with her.

The two returned along the route they came, maintaining silence throughout.

It wasn't until they arrived at the abandoned alchemy room that Su Qingyao stopped.

"The formation foundation is destroyed, so there will be no trapping formation in tomorrow's finals." She turned around, her gaze falling on Chen Ji's face, "But Han Lie's strength cannot be underestimated. Are you certain you still want to participate?"

Chen Ji smiled, that smile carrying a hint of cunning: "Since the traps are gone, why wouldn't I participate?"

He paused, his gaze directly meeting Su Qingyao's eyes: "As for senior sister... you've helped me so much tonight. I haven't yet asked—why are you helping me?"

Inside the alchemy room, the candlelight flickered.

Su Qingyao stood by the window, moonlight outlining her cold, serene silhouette. She remained silent for a long while, long enough that Chen Ji thought she wouldn't answer.

"Because of your father."

These words were like a thunderclap, exploding in Chen Ji's heart.

His expression froze for an instant, then returned to normal: "My father... what connection does he have with senior sister?"

Su Qingyao turned around, her face in the moonlight carrying a hint of softness she had never shown before.

"Chen Ji, there are some things..." She took a deep breath, "I shouldn't tell you now. But since you asked..."

She paused, her eyes flashing with complex emotions.

"After tomorrow's finals, I will tell you everything."

Chen Ji watched her quietly.

This woman who had always been as cold as ice, her gaze now carried a hint of... anticipation?

What was she anticipating?

"Very well." Chen Ji nodded, "Then I shall await senior sister's good news."

He rose and walked toward the door. When he reached the threshold, he suddenly stopped.

"By the way, senior sister." He didn't turn around, "That white figure tonight... it wasn't one of yours, was it?"

Behind him, there was a moment of silence.

"...No." Su Qingyao's voice carried a hint of confusion, "I'm also wondering, who was it?"

The corner of Chen Ji's mouth slightly lifted.

It seemed someone else was watching over him from the shadows.

How interesting.

Chen Ji walked out of the alchemy room, the night wind brushing against his face, carrying a chill.

He looked up at the sky, the crescent moon like a hook, the stars sparse and few.

Too much had happened tonight—the threatening letter, the trapping formation, Han Lie's murderous intent, Su Qingyao's secrets...

At every step, someone was setting up a game; at every step, hidden killing intent lurked.

But what of it?

A cold smile curled at the corner of Chen Ji's lips. Since they wanted him dead, he would survive just to spite them. Not only would he survive, but he would make those vermin hiding in the shadows pay the price.

The Tianji Record Fragment in his embrace grew faintly warm, as if responding to his will.

"Tomorrow's finals, Han Lie..." Chen Ji murmured, his eyes flashing with cold light, "I will let you know what a true genius is."

The night wind blew past, carrying away his voice.

Tomorrow, the winds of change would rise.
